title: Excise Tax on Remittance Transfers (Proposed Rule, IRC Section 4475)
date_evidence: A Proposed Rule by the Internal Revenue Service on 04/13/2026 (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/04/13)
key_claim: Treasury and the IRS issued proposed regulations implementing IRC Section 4475, the new 1% federal excise tax on remittance transfers occurring after 31 December 2025; the tax applies to transfers funded with cash, a money order, a cashier's check or a similar physical instrument, and is collected by the remittance transfer provider.
notes: Tier 1 primary regulatory document. Anchors the tax mechanics and the post-31-Dec-2025 effective date.

title: Remittance Transfers in 2025: The Year in Review
key_claim: In 2025 most of Latin America and the Caribbean registered the highest remittance growth in 20 years (nine countries originating over 90% of flows received US$158 billion), but the growth was driven by migrants' precautionary risk-mitigation - a 27% increase in the average amount remitted ahead of possible deportation - not by new migration; with declining migration and rising deportations, 2026 regional growth is projected below 2%.
verbatim_quote: increased the average amount remitted by 27 percent as a precaution
notes: Structural anchor: canonical primary research (Manuel Orozco) on the LAC remittance sender base, deportation effect and 2026 outlook. 3-6 month band, cited inline like any other source.

title: Latin America and the Caribbean Economic Update, April 2026: Slow Growth amid Global Uncertainty and Weak Investment
date_evidence: Latin America and the Caribbean Economic Update - April 2026
key_claim: Regional GDP growth in Latin America and the Caribbean is projected at 2.1% in 2026, below the 2.4% recorded in 2025, with downward revisions for several economies; private consumption remains the main driver but its impulse is modest as real incomes recover only gradually.
notes: Tier 2 institutional report. Used for recipient-economy macro fragility context, not for a remittance-specific figure.

title: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with Honduras on the Fourth and Fifth Reviews of the ECF and EFF
key_claim: Honduras - one of the most remittance-dependent economies in Central America - remains under an IMF Extended Credit Facility and Extended Fund Facility programme; staff and the authorities reached a staff-level agreement on the fourth and fifth reviews, with Board approval expected in late June 2026 to make about US$245 million available.
notes: Tier 1 primary source. Used to show a remittance-dependent Central American sovereign is under active IMF programme monitoring; remittance-dependency framing is analyst synthesis.

title: Remittances to Mexico rebound after declining throughout 2025
key_claim: Banco de Mexico data show Mexico received US$14.45 billion in remittances in Q1 2026, up 1.4% year-on-year and a record first quarter, but the number of individual transfers fell 4% year-on-year while the average transfer rose to US$405; remittances had fallen 4.6% in 2025, the worst annual decline in 16 years.
notes: Tier 3 journalism reporting Banco de Mexico Q1 2026 data. Counter-evidence: headline value rose even as transaction count fell.

title: IRS releases proposed rules for remittance excise tax
key_claim: The 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act created a new 1% excise tax on certain remittance transfers occurring after 31 December 2025; the tax applies to transfers initiated by a domestic sender and received outside the US when funded with cash, a money order, a cashier's check or a similar physical instrument.
notes: Tier 3 professional-services alert corroborating the Tier 1 regulatory source on tax scope.

publisher: Americas Society / Council of the Americas
title: IMF and World Bank's April 2026 Update: Latin America's Economic Outlook
key_claim: The IMF April 2026 World Economic Outlook and the World Bank April 2026 LAC update both show subdued Latin American growth; net energy importers such as Central America and the Caribbean stand to see growth diminished by global shocks, leaving little fiscal buffer.
notes: Tier 3 regional analysis organisation; macro-context corroboration.
